thread:
maria-support: Customer (ACME) filed an escalation — their engineer reports they can no longer access some projects in the console after an Okta group rename. They see a 403 when opening Project > Settings > Members, but API calls using the same user token to list projects succeed. Can someone triage?

ajay-eng: ACK, can you paste the console error and the user email/org/project IDs? Also, did they recently rename the SCIM group in Okta or delete+recreate?
\bmaria-support: Here's the info from the customer: email: carla@acme.com, org_id: org_01G8Y2Z, project_id: proj_0a9bC3, timestamp: 2026-03-12T15:02Z. They said the identity team renamed the group in Okta yesterday (changed display name and group external id). They did NOT delete the user.
\ben-cs: Customer pasted the console error screenshot: it shows a red banner "Permission denied (403)" when opening Members. In network tab the call is: GET https://console.redwood.ai/api/orgs/org_01G8Y2Z/projects/proj_0a9bC3/members  -> 403.
\maria-support: Customer also ran curl with the same session token and got a 403 for the console endpoint: ```curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <user-token>" -v "https://console.redwood.ai/api/orgs/org_01G8Y2Z/projects/proj_0a9bC3/members" 
< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{"error":"permission_denied","message":"403 Not authorized"}```

ajay-eng: That matches the console. Two odd things: they can list projects via API (GET /orgs/org_01G8Y2Z/projects) — so org-level read is fine — but project-level members endpoint denies. That looks like role binding for that project lost or group membership not reflected at project scope after the SCIM group rename.
\linda-identity: SCIM note: when a group is deleted and recreated (or externalId changes), Okta will create a new group id. Our group->project role mappings use the SCIM group.id for role bindings unless there is a stable externalId mapping. If the externalId changed, the platform may treat it as a different group and not reapply bindings to projects, leaving members effectively unbound at project scope.
\ajay-eng: Quick repro steps for our triage: 1) get the affected user id: GET /v1/admin/users?email=carla@acme.com 2) check effective role bindings: GET /v1/admin/role_bindings?subject=user:carla@acme.com&scope=project:proj_0a9bC3 3) check group bindings: GET /v1/admin/role_bindings?subject=group:<old-scim-group-id> and group:<new-scim-group-id>
\maria-support: Customer can't access admin endpoints. I've asked them to share the role_binding query output if they can, but they prefer us to run checks since it's an escalation.
\ops-bot: Incident created: SUP-2026-3849. Notifying eng-identity and eng-platform oncall.
\ajay-eng: I pulled the role bindings for that project — looks like there is a binding for group:scim-GROUP-111 (old id) granting role project:viewer, but no binding for scim-GROUP-205 (new id). The user is a member of the new group id only. So effective membership at project scope is gone.
\linda-identity: Root cause: Okta rename changed the group's externalId, and identity team used the "recreate group" flow which produced a new SCIM id. Our SCIM sync created a new group in Redwood rather than mapping to the old. We need to map the old role_bindings to the new group id.
\ajay-eng: Short-term workaround for the customer: add Carla as a direct project member (invite by email) or grant the new SCIM group a project role manually in Console -> Project -> Roles. That will restore their access immediately. Long-term fix: migrate bindings.
\maria-support: Customer accepted workaround for now (direct project invite). They asked for permanent fix to avoid repeat.
\linda-identity: I'll run a migration: steps I'm taking now: 1) find matching group by displayName and externalId delta 2) reassign role_bindings from old_scim_id -> new_scim_id via admin script 3) run a SCIM resync and validate effective members. Admin commands I'm running internally: ```# list group bindings for org
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/admin/role_bindings?org=org_01G8Y2Z&subject_type=group&project=proj_0a9bC3"
# reassign binding (internal tool)
POST /v1/admin/internal/migrate-group-binding {"org":"org_01G8Y2Z","from_group":"scim-GROUP-111","to_group":"scim-GROUP-205"}```
\ajay-eng: After migrate, I'll run the access-check helper: POST /v1/admin/simulate_access {"user":"carla@acme.com","resource":"project:proj_0a9bC3","action":"view_members"} to confirm.
\ops-bot: Update: internal job completed (job id job_9832).
\linda-identity: Migration done. I reattached role_bindings from scim-GROUP-111 -> scim-GROUP-205 and triggered a SCIM delta sync.
\ajay-eng: Ran simulate_access and got success. Also retried the console members endpoint with the customer's token; now returns 200 and member list. Carla confirmed via chat she can see Members and manage invites.
\maria-support: Customer confirmed resolution and asked for a root-cause summary and prevention guidance. I shared: 1) Avoid delete+recreate SCIM groups in Okta; prefer rename with stable externalId when possible. 2) If group recreation is needed, coordinate with Redwood identity to migrate bindings (SUP-2026-3849). 3) As a fallback, invite affected users directly to the project.
\ben-cs: Customer appreciated the fast workaround and the migration. Marking ticket resolved. :tada:
\maria-support: Closing thread, file note to update docs: add a KB article about SCIM group recreation impact + migration steps.
\ops-bot: Ticket SUP-2026-3849 -> status: resolved.
